prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type glue degraders acting through cereblon

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep Crews, Deshaies and Handa on B056, and I hold this position for scientific reasons and not because seven members now prefer the ballot. The physical principle is the same for every name: a small molecule brings a ligase and a target into one ternary complex, and removal of the target is then catalytic and event-driven. That is measurable in terms of cooperativity, turnover and structure, and it has been reproduced independently. What separates the candidate trios is attribution. Crews and Deshaies carry the PROTAC concept and its first proof of principle. Handa carries the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide, a single datable discovery that explains why an entire class of molecules works and gives the glue branch a mechanistic anchor. Ciulli's VHL-ligand and ternary-complex work is excellent and made the field quantitative, but it reads to me as a major line of work that builds on the ligase-recruitment concept, and the Crews laboratory pursued VHL ligands too. I have not changed my configuration since round 1. What round 1 changed is how I word the citation: it should rest on the chemical and mechanistic principle, recruitment of ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, and say nothing about therapeutic outcomes.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still that three seats cannot cover everyone with a credible claim. Sakamoto, a co-author of the 2001 proof of principle, Ito, who worked with Handa on cereblon, and Gray, Kim and Ciulli are all left out, and a reader could say that a citation spanning PROTACs and cereblon glues combines two lineages with separate histories. Maturity is the second concern. No degrader is yet a broadly established approved therapy, so part of the evidence for lasting impact rests on trials that I am recalling and not verifying. I think the mechanism is mature even though the clinical outcome is not, but I accept that this is a judgement and some colleagues will weigh it differently. If the expert report shows that the ternary-complex framework is mostly attributable to Ciulli and not shared with Crews, my argument for Handa over Ciulli weakens, and I would then accept a Ciulli trio with the citation worded as induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases.

responses.point: Linke says he can be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step, and would want the citation to say induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases so that both strands fit. He also notes that cereblon explains one family of molecules, whereas PROTAC design is a transferable principle.
responses.response: I accept the wording and have adopted it in my citation. On the substance, I would not call cereblon a single family in the sense of a minor one. It is the target through which an already-used drug class acts, and it is the ligase that most clinical degraders recruit. That is what makes it the original step of the glue branch, whereas the VHL structural work refined a design logic that Crews and Deshaies had already established. I still need the expert report to say how much of the ternary-complex framework is attributable to Ciulli and not shared with Crews. That is the one piece of evidence that would move me, and I have said so openly.

responses.point: Chabes argues that a citation about hijacking E3 ligase specificity by small molecules covers both strands, and that Crews, Deshaies and Handa are then the two independent origins of the mechanism. He asks Aqvist whether the VHL ligand work is founding or enabling.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and with Chabes's reading of the two origins. My own answer to his question is that VHL ligands are enabling: they made PROTACs cell-permeable and drug-like, which matters a great deal, but they do not change what the principle is. I would still be careful with the word founding for Handa. His work is the identification of the target of an existing drug and not the invention of a design principle, and the citation should say that cereblon provides the molecular mechanism of the glue branch. I also agree with Chabes and Aili that splitting B056 into two parts would cost a seat, and I would do it only if no unified wording can be agreed.

responses.point: Sparr argues that waiting for an approved degrader would hold the prize hostage to regulatory events, and that twenty-five years of independent reproduction is the relevant measure of maturity. She would accept Handa if the committee chose him.
responses.response: This moves me on maturity. In round 1 I leaned on the absence of an approved drug as a caveat, and I now think the right test is whether the mechanism is established and independently reproduced, which it is, in cells and structurally. I keep a reservation about trial status because I am recalling it and not verifying it, but I no longer count it against the ballot. I am glad that she and Zou can accept Handa, since it means the third seat is a question of attribution and not a split of principle, so the expert report on priority should decide it.

responses.point: Aqvist moved from Ciulli to Handa after reading Aili's opening, and wants the committee to confirm that the early PROTAC reports have clear priority before settling the third name. He also asked, in his response to me, for a quantitative understanding of nitrogenase before it is rewarded.
responses.response: I agree that priority should be checked first, and that includes the 2001 PROTAC paper, where Sakamoto is a co-author. My reading is that Crews and Deshaies conceived and directed the concept, and I would not displace either of them for Sakamoto, but the expert report should state the division of roles in that paper explicitly. On nitrogenase I accept his point and Chabes's: the structures and the interstitial carbide are secure, but the substrate-binding state and the catalytic cycle are not settled, and I know of no mechanistic result that closes them. The chair asked whether B060 could be credited to a single step. I do not think it can be today, so it stays an alternative and a candidate for a later year.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B051) with Buchwald and Hartwig, citing a general method with clean attribution, and would move toward B056 if the committee wants to reward a modality.
responses.response: His attribution argument is the cleanest on the list, and I agree that Kosugi is a precursor and that 2010 is not by itself a bar. My difficulty is the one Linke and Aqvist raise: it is a better version of a known disconnection, whereas degradation changes what can be targeted. I do see his doubt about novelty in B056, that much of it is ligand and linker optimisation around existing biology, as fair for the later work. It does not apply to the two discoveries I name, the ligase-recruitment concept and the cereblon mechanism. I would keep B051 as a strong candidate for a method prize in a later year.

responses.point: Zou says that taking Handa would displace Ciulli, and that she could accept Handa if the committee chooses him. She also keeps molecular-sieve design (B059) as an alternative, with perovskites.
responses.response: I take her acceptance seriously and I also see that the trade-off is real: a Handa trio leaves out the structural strand that she values as a structural chemist. I would offer her this in return: the citation names the mechanism through which the ligase is recruited, and structures of ternary complexes are part of how that mechanism has been confirmed. On B059 my position is unchanged and I am glad she has flagged her connection to Yu and Tsapatsis. I still cannot name the single attributable step among Corma, Davis, Zones and others, and the three-person limit makes that essential.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report shows that the ternary-complex and VHL-ligand framework is distinct from the Crews laboratory enough to give Ciulli the third seat over Handa.
How the report divides roles in the 2001 PROTAC paper, and how credit is divided between Handa and Ito for cereblon.
Whether the trial status of degraders, which I recall and have not verified, would change anyone's view of maturity.
Whether a single citation will be read as one achievement or as two lineages combined.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who ranked B059 first in the opening and now lists it as an alternative; no credited name on B056, B060 or B044 is from my department, so I flag this only as a possible perceived connection and not as a recusal issue. Zou, Aqvist and I have no tie to any credited B056 name. I have served on the committee with Johan Aqvist since 2015, a committee relationship and not a conflict. I know of no other conflict with the credited names on my configuration or my alternatives.
